newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels claim new successes in northern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rebels claim new successes in northern Zaire.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Wednesday his forces had set off in the direction of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko's jungle palace at Gbadolite after capturing the key town of Isiro in north east Zaire.
Zaire denied the fall of Isiro but acknowledged that heavy fighting was taking place around the town, saying it was "seriously threatened".

In Paris, a French Foreign Ministry spokesman said the rebels, who hold towns and territory in east Zaire, would be excluded from an international conference which France wants organised on the Zaire crisis.

"Our forces are now in complete control of Isiro. The town was taken late on Tuesday," Kabila said. Rebel officials said Kabila's units were on Wednesday conducting mop-up operations in Isiro and had completely seized its airstrip.
Later, hundreds of newly trained recruits joined the rebel ranks in the town of Uvira, bordering Burundi, the third such parade in the rebel-held east within a week.
"Our struggle will continue until Mobutu is killed," sang the rebels, wearing U.S.-style combat uniforms, wellington boots and carrying rifles. They lauded Kabila in other war songs.
Some 1,200 newly trained recruits marched in Bukavu on Tuesday and 5,000 in Goma last Thursday as part of a well-organised campaign to show off the alliance's strength.

Kabila said government troops and foreign mercenaries had retreated from Isiro to Buta, the next stop on the road towards Mobutu's multi-million-dollar residence. Isiro is about 800 km (500 miles) east of Gbadolite.

"Our advance has caused a lot of panic in the government. The panic is such that Mobutu now sleeps in Bangui (Central African Republic's capital) and only comes to Gbadolite in the morning," Kabila added.

In the capital Kinshasa, a senior government defence official said the rebels had captured the town of Bafwasende in eastern Zaire and described Isiro as under serious threat. Kabila told Reuters his forces took Bafwasende on Sunday.
Isiro, a hub connecting routes to Uganda, Sudan and the Central African Republic, was a key base for the army and mercenaries.

The Kinshasa official said a cargo plane carrying fresh Ugandan troops to fight alongside the rebels had crashed inside Zaire's border killing some of those on board. Zairean troops had taken prisoner survivors, he added.
Uganda denied knowledge of any such crash. Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of invading to back the rebels.

The rebels, who launched the war in October accusing the Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship, have given Mobutu, who had prostate surgery in Europe in August, until February 21 to begin talks on stepping down.

Kabila said no one had so far solicited his views on how to resolve the conflict in Africa's third largest country, yet his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) was the major player. "We are part of the Zaire game, yet no one bothers to invite us to regional meetings on Zaire."
In Paris, Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters who asked him if the rebels would be invited:
"This is a conference to be attended by states and which is to be organised by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity."
